veil-v2-hovers.detail: Light pressure (0.0174 m/s²) and Venus's gravity both point toward Venus; the shade falls with 0.0347 m/s² and reaches Venus in about 1 d.

veil-hovers.detail: At 1.11 × 10⁶ km sunward of Venus the forces on a Veil with a lightness of 0.0077 balance. The point is unstable along the Sun line, so holding it takes constant trimming, by tilting slats, which the model does not size.

veil-leak-fits.detail: Gaps of 0.05% plus 0.03% through the closed slats, against the 0.1% the closed Veil may let through.

exhaust-fits-venus.detail: The lit tiles throw out 2.2 × 10²⁰ W at 1.3 MW/m², and only 50% of them are lit at once, so the tiles cover 72% of Venus: 83% of the band within 60° of the equator, which leaves the poles to the falling ice.

second-law.detail: The pumps reach 50% of the Carnot limit, so the model charges 1.09 × 10²⁸ J of work for 5.3 × 10²⁶ J of heat, more than the 2.0 × 10²⁷ J even a reversible pump would need if every joule left from 737 K.

exhaust-spares-veil.detail: Seen from Venus the Veil is 0.68° in radius, so the lit tiles send it 0.007% of their light: 1.5 × 10¹⁶ W at the Exhaust's peak, 5.1% of the 3.0 × 10¹⁷ W of sunlight it turns away. It pushes the Veil toward the Sun, against the sunlight, and the slats that trim its station take it up.

exhaust-pump-photons.detail: Pumped at 2.5 µm, below the tiles' 0.54 eV bandgap, each photon leaves at least 0.54 eV plus the heat of the tile it crossed. From the hottest starting air a joule of pumping light can carry 0.26 J of heat; the model has it carry 0.12 J, and less as the air cools.

graphite-for-caps.detail: 4.6 × 10¹⁷ kg of graphite by the end of sealing; the caps need 2.5 × 10¹⁷ kg.

ice-arrives.detail: Launches run from 9 October 2033 to 7 January 2034. The slowest transfer takes 410 d, and the last Brick falls into the air on 23 January 2035, before the pumps stop with the last caps on 1 September 2036. Its heat is the pumps' to take out.

ceres-ground-heat.detail: All the heat made at Ceres is 6.6 times what its whole surface could radiate at 1,500 K (8.0 × 10¹⁷ W), so the Crown sheds it in space; the barrels leave 6.3 × 10¹⁵ W on the ground, radiators over 0.79% of the surface.

ceres-receiver-cooling.detail: At 40 MW/m² each square metre of receiver hands 10 MW/m² to its coolant, against the 10 MW/m² ITER's divertor is built to carry; left to radiate it alone, a receiver would reach 3,100 K.

crown-orbit.detail: The Crown circles at 1,190 km and its fins reach 2,100 km, well inside half of Ceres's 220,000 km Hill radius, where orbits around a small body stay bound; Ceres's recoil, 9.1 × 10⁻⁷ m/s², is small beside its 0.014 m/s² pull even at the fins' edge.

crown-tethers.detail: Summed from the surface to the Crown, Ceres's net pull on a tether is 59 kJ/kg, against the 3.9 MJ/kg carbon fibre holds at full strength; hanging the 8.1 × 10¹¹ kg of cables and holding the beams' 2.8 × 10¹⁰ N push takes 1.8 × 10¹⁰ kg of fibre.

ceres-ready-in-time.detail: The seed leaves Earth on 1 October 2028, with the Foundry's once Ouroboros-0 has passed, and lands on 16 January 2030; doubling every 45 d, the factories finish the 6.5 × 10¹³ kg of Railheads and Crown on 2 June 2033, against a first launch on 9 October 2033.

railheads-within-lattice.detail: Throwing 1.0 × 10¹⁸ kg in 0.25 yr takes 6.3 × 10¹⁸ W, which Ceres's receivers make from 8.4 × 10¹⁸ W of the Lattice's 2.2 × 10²⁰ W.

ceres-clear-of-jupiter.detail: At its new aphelion Ceres stays 2.18 AU inside Jupiter's closest approach to the Sun, 6.1 of Jupiter's Hill radii against the 2√3 that keeps two orbits from meeting; its Tisserand parameter falls from 3.31 to 3.31, still above the 3 below which Jupiter takes control.

foundry-affords-veil.detail: The Foundry stands still for 9.8 d to build the 5.4 × 10¹¹ kg Veil, whose last parts leave Mercury on 16 September 2032; one doubling is 60 d.

foundry-size.detail: After 28 doublings the 2.7 × 10¹⁴ kg Foundry builds the 1.2 × 10¹⁴ kg Lattice in 39 d and the 1.9 × 10¹⁴ kg of hardware at Venus in 61 d: both done 1780 days after landing, against 1821 with one doubling fewer and 1790 with one more.

aegis-structure.detail: The coil's field pulls on its winding with 1.2 × 10¹¹ N; holding it takes at least 2.0 × 10¹¹ kg of carbon fibre at full strength, 0.063 days of the full Foundry's output against the 60 d of one doubling.

forges-on-seas.detail: The Forges float on the seas from April 2035; the Clear Rain begins for good on January 2035.

traj-heat-books.detail: The Exhaust lifts 7.3 × 10²⁶ J: Venus's 5.3 × 10²⁶ J, less the 1.6 × 10²¹ J still held by the CO₂ the Frost Towers leave in the air, plus 2.0 × 10²⁶ J that enters while the pumps run. The two sides agree to rounding. This confirms the simulation's own bookkeeping; a heat source the simulation leaves out cannot show here.

frozen-before-sealing.detail: The simulated seas are frozen through on 30 April 2036, leaving 120 d to the last cap on 1 September 2036: the crawler-rafts must lay 1.2 × 10⁶ km²/d.

frost-before-sealing.detail: The simulated Frost Towers finish on 26 June 2036; the last caps are sealed on 1 September 2036.

genesis-by-deadline.detail: Seeding waits for the oxygen (30 September 2036) and for the seas to hold their pH (1 December 2036), so it begins on 1 December 2036; doubling every 1 d, the cells reach bloom density on 12 December 2036, against a deadline of 31 December 2036.

earth-like-by-deadline.detail: The day-by-day simulation reaches Earth-like conditions on 30 September 2036, 92 d before the 31 December 2036 deadline. The chimneys, not the power, set the pace on 51 d of it.

ozone-model-earth.detail: 280 DU against 279 DU from a three-dimensional model of the pre-industrial Earth, within a quarter either way, with nothing fitted.

ozone-shield-in-time.detail: One day of sunlight makes 49.9 DU, easily measured. The column reaches 185 DU on 2 December 2036, 91 d after the Veil opens, so lichens and mosses go onto land from 2 December 2036, against a deadline of 31 December 2036.

energy-closes.detail: The Lattice beams 2.2 × 10²⁸ J from full power to the deadline, against 1.6 × 10²⁸ J the plan needs: 30% spare.
